standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the construction of beta in the counted proof (lines 2698-2699)
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the domain of the adjunction map an S-module, so that an S-module map out of it can be tested on the tensor product.

standard_prerequisites.name: The pure tensor m tensor 1 as the natural image of an element
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the reverse construction beta'(m) = beta(m tensor 1).

core_obligations: Given an R-module map alpha from M to N restricted, define alpha' on the tensor product by alpha'(m tensor s) = s alpha(m) and check it is well defined and S-linear (proof lines 2696-2698).
Given an S-module map beta out of M tensor S, define beta' by beta'(m) = beta(m tensor 1) (proof lines 2698-2700).
The two constructions are mutually inverse; the author states this verification as omitted (proof line 2701).
proof_roadmap: Write both directions of the adjunction, testing the forward one on pure tensors and the backward one at m tensor 1 (proof lines 2695-2700).
Leave the mutual-inverse check to the reader, as the author does (proof line 2701).
difficulty_reason: For a ring map from R to S the lemma states that base change from R-modules to S-modules is left adjoint to restriction of scalars (statement lines 2684-2693). The proof writes the two directions on elements: alpha goes to the S-linear map sending m tensor s to s alpha(m), and beta goes to the map sending m to beta(m tensor 1) (proof lines 2695-2700). The only part not written out is that these are mutually inverse, which the author explicitly marks as omitted and which is a routine computation on pure tensors; the constructions themselves, including the well-definedness of the first one, are given. H2.
